e-13933.knowledge_point: Compound Inequalities That Require Flipping the Inequality Sign
e-13933.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & <-2x+1\le 7 \\ -1-1 & <-2x+1-1\le 7-1 \\ -2 & <-2x\le 6\end{aligned}
$$

At this point, we need to divide by $-2$. However, because we are dividing by a negative, we also need to flip the inequality signs.

$$
\begin{aligned}-2 & <-2x\le 6 \\ \frac{-2}{-2} & \,>\,\frac{-2x}{-2}\,\ge \,\frac{6}{-2} \\ 1 & >x\ge -3\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $1 > x \geq - 3,$ but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers:

$$
-3 \leq x < 1
$$

e-13935.problem: Represent the solution to the inequality $-3 < 1-2x < 11$ using a number line.
e-13935.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual. 

First, we apply the addition principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3 & <1-2x<11 \\ -3-1 & <1-2x-1<11-1 \\ -4 & <-2x<10\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-2.$ Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality signs. 

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & <-2x<10 \\ \frac{-4}{-2} & >\frac{-2x}{-2}>\frac{10}{-2} \\ 2 & >x>-5\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $2 > x > -5$, but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers: 

$$
-5 < x < 2
$$

$$

Question 8
?

What is the solution to −3<5−2x≤1?

a
−4<x≤−2
b
−4≤x<−2
c
2<x≤4
d
2≤x<4
e
−2<x≤4
Submit

decision.explanation: Subtract 5 to get -8<-2x≤-4. Divide by -2 and reverse both inequality signs: 4>x≥2. Thus 2≤x<4, option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual. 

First, we apply the addition principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3 & <5-2x\le 1 \\ -3-5 & <5-2x-5\le 1-5 \\ -8 & <-2x\le -4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-2.$ Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality signs.

 

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & <-2x\le -4 \\ \frac{-8}{-2} & >x\ge \frac{-4}{-2} \\ 4 & >x\ge 2\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $4>x\ge 2$, but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers: $2\le x<4.$

after.worked_solution:

$$

$$
-5\le x<7

b

decision.explanation: Subtract 6 to get -5≤-2x≤2. Divide by -2, reversing both inequality signs: 5/2≥x≥-1. Thus -1≤x≤5/2, option e.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual. 

First, we apply the addition principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & \le -2x+6\le 8 \\ 1-6 & \le -2x+6-6\le 8-6 \\ -5 & \le -2x\le 2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-2.$ Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality signs.

$$
\begin{aligned}-5 & \le -2x\le 2 \\ \frac{-5}{-2} & \ge \frac{-2x}{-2}\ge \frac{2}{-2} \\ \frac{5}{2} & \ge x\ge -1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $\frac{5}{2}\ge x\ge -1$, but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers: 

$$
-1\le x\le \frac{5}{2}
$$

b
−2≤x≤12
c
−2≤x≤4

−52≤x≤1

−1≤x≤52

We isolate x by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual.

First, we apply the addition principle: 1≤−2x+6≤81−6≤−2x+6−6≤8−6−5≤−2x≤2

Then, we divide by −2. Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality signs.

−5≤−2x≤2−5−2≥−2x−2≥2−252≥x≥−1 The solution can be written as 52≥x≥−1, but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers:

−1≤x≤52

after.problem: Which of the following number lines gives the solution to $-9<6-5x<1?$
after.worked_solution:
We isolate $x$ by applying the addition and multiplication principles, as usual. 

First, we apply the addition principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}-9 & <6-5x<1 \\ -9-6 & <6-5x-6<1-6 \\ -15 & <-5x<-5\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we divide by $-5.$ Note that since we are dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality signs. 

$$
\begin{aligned}-15 & <-5x<-5 \\ \frac{-15}{-5} & >\frac{-5x}{-5}>\frac{-5}{-5} \\ 3 & >x>1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution can be written as $3>x>1$, but this is somewhat difficult to read because the larger number is on the left rather than the right. So, we will rewrite the solution by reversing the order of the numbers: 

$$
1<x<3
$$
